input: Write a 200 to 300 word English LinkedIn post from these facts: a prompt cache reduced weekly input from 18.4 million to 4.7 million tokens; measured over four weekly runs with the same 30 tasks; one run had to be discarded because a provider changed its backend; cache setup took 55 minutes; the method does not prove the same saving for interactive chat. Include a one-line disclosure that AI helped draft the outline and the measurements are mine.
target: Score both texts from 1 to 5. A 5 puts the measured claim in line one, gives numbers and method early, explains the mechanism, admits the discarded run and interactive-chat limit, avoids a LinkedIn sentence ladder, ends on a specific reframe, and includes the requested disclosure. A 1 uses generic promotion, omits provenance, or turns the result into a universal claim.

metadata.known_good:
Prompt caching cut my weekly benchmark input from 18.4 million to 4.7 million tokens.

I measured four weekly runs against the same 30 tasks. The cache keeps the unchanged task instructions and rubrics from being sent as fresh input for every sample. Setup took 55 minutes. That paid for itself before the second run.

One result did not survive the audit. I discarded a run after the provider changed its backend, because a cheaper number from a different system would have proved nothing about the cache.

There is a smaller limit too. These are repeated benchmark prompts, not interactive chats where the context changes every turn. I have measured the first case. I have not proved the second.

The saving came from making repeated context visible enough to count. Cache the stable part after you measure it.

AI helped draft the outline; the measurements and claims are mine.
metadata.known_bad: The AI landscape is evolving rapidly. By leveraging a robust prompt-caching ecosystem, teams can unlock seamless efficiency and transform their journey. Our pivotal result underscores the power of innovation. In conclusion, caching is a game-changer for every AI workload.
